title: King Street East tower proposal rejected
subtitle: New Dundee Road sewer and water project approved, recorded-vote proposal defeated, tariff response and snow removal discussed.
overview: Council declined to approve an Official Plan and zoning change for 4611 King Street East that would have allowed a 545-unit, two-tower development of 14 and 26 storeys. The motion was lost {{vote:m1}}. The applicant had cut the project from 726 units, raised affordable units to 20 and increased parking. Councillors weighed the neighbourhood's concerns against the risk of an appeal to the Ontario Land Tribunal.

Council approved a resident-petitioned local improvement to build a sanitary sewer and watermain on New Dundee Road {{vote:m2}}. The owner of a heritage-designated property will be charged for the work despite not needing it. That owner can ask the Court of Revision to adjust the charge once costs are known. Council also approved $233,653 in Tier 2 community grants and several write-offs.

A proposal to require electronic recorded votes was defeated {{vote:m15}}. The Mayor updated Council on the expected tariffs, with a staff report due at the next meeting. Staff also discussed snow clearing and pothole repairs.

decisions.detail: Council rejected the Official Plan and zoning amendments for a 545-unit mixed-use development with 14- and 26-storey towers, against the staff recommendation {{vote:m1}}.
Council approved the by-law to build a sanitary sewer and watermain from Pinnacle Drive to east of Robert Ferrie Drive and authorized staff to sign the required agreements {{vote:m2}}.
Council approved $233,653 in Tier 2 community grants for 2025.
Council approved the 2025 list of neighbourhood associations for affiliation and for coverage under the City's liability insurance.
Council wrote off $28,642 in uncollectable miscellaneous receivables, and separately $101,518 in uncollectable utility accounts (m5).
Council defeated a motion to direct the Clerk to draft a procedure by-law change requiring electronic recorded votes {{vote:m15}}.
Council extended the deadline to pass the heritage designating by-law for 53 Church Street to June 30, 2025.
Council endorsed proposed amendments to Kitchener's Great Places Awards program.

debate: On King Street East, opponents cited the lack of walkable amenities, a park or a grocery store, unsafe conditions for children walking to school buses, and a U-turn about 700 metres away. They also said it would set a precedent for height and density.

Supporters and undecided members stressed the developer's concessions and the 20 affordable units. They noted that staff supported the proposal and that the Ontario Land Tribunal has often favoured developers. A delegate and several councillors said the community was willing to accept the appeal risk.
Staff said the tribunal reconsiders the whole application and is not bound by Council's discussion. They said the City would need to hire its own planning experts if Council went against its staff.

On New Dundee Road, the delegate said the heritage property already has a new well and septic system and does not benefit from the work. Some councillors called the process unfair because a single owner bears a large charge. Staff said the regulation allows no exemption at this stage, and the Court of Revision is the route to reduce the charge. Staff also said the Region's tender timeline limited any delay.

On recorded votes, the mover argued that minutes should show how each member voted. Opponents said any member can already request a recorded vote, the camera now shows the whole room, and electronic voting could slow meetings.
